sourcedFrom: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision (2024 copyright line; 2025 file)
cleanIntro: A direct-impingement AR from a maker that says plainly why it fouls: gas is siphoned off the barrel into the upper receiver and the carrier key, so carbon builds up in several places, and ⛔ BUSHMASTER NAMES EXCESSIVE CARBON AS THE LEADING CAUSE OF MALFUNCTIONS IN ANY AR. Its interval is every 500 rounds — and as little as 100 with poor ammunition. ⛔ Two hard prohibitions ride with it: NO FOAM CLEANERS, and never dry-fire with the upper and lower apart, because the steel hammer strikes the aluminium magazine well.

steps.title: Selector to SAFE, magazine out
steps.action: Muzzle safe. Put the selector on SAFE — if the hammer is not cocked it will not go there. Then depress the magazine release and pull the magazine out of the bottom of the well.
steps.prose: Bushmaster prints the hammer-cocked caveat right in the step, which is the useful place for it.
steps.quote: Place the firearm on "SAFE" as shown in the picture. If the hammer is not cocked, the lever cannot be pointed toward safe.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Unloading Your firearm, printed p.13

steps.title: Bolt locked open, then look AND feel
steps.action: Pull the charging handle rearward, press the bottom of the bolt catch and let the bolt come forward onto it, then return the charging handle fully forward. Look through the ejection port into the chamber — and verify with a tool or, carefully, a finger.
steps.prose: ⛔ Bushmaster asks for a PHYSICAL check as well as a visual one. On a dark chamber with brass-coloured light that is the difference between thinking it is empty and knowing.
steps.quote: Visually and physically verify with a tool, or if no tool is available, carefully use your finger, to ensure that there is not a round of ammunition in the chamber.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Unloading Your firearm, printed p.13

steps.title: ⛔ Fingers OUT of the ejection port
steps.action: With the rifle clear, push the top of the bolt catch firmly and make sure the bolt is forward. Keep your fingers away from the ejection port while you do it.
steps.prose: ⛔ The carrier runs forward under full spring force. Bushmaster warns about it because it takes a fingertip off, not because it pinches.
steps.quote: Never allow a finger to enter the ejection port while the bolt catch is depressed. The bolt carrier will slide forward with considerable force and may cause serious injury.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Field Stripping Your Firearm, printed pp.14-19
steps.warn: Wear safety glasses when field stripping the firearm.

steps.title: Takedown pin left to right, then pivot the upper open
steps.action: Push the takedown pin from the LEFT so it slides out to the right. It is designed to stop just short of falling out. The upper will then pivot forward.
steps.prose: ⛔ And once it is open, never pull the trigger. Bushmaster spells out the damage: the steel hammer hits the rear of the aluminium magazine well.
steps.quote: Push the take down pin on the left side so that it will slide out to the right side. The pin is designed to stop its travel just short of falling completely out.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Field Stripping Your Firearm, printed pp.14-19
steps.warn: Never dry fire the firearm when the upper and lower are not fully assembled. The steel hammer will hit the rear of the aluminum magazine well and eventually cause damage.

steps.title: Pivot pin too, if you want them fully apart
steps.action: Push the pivot pin left to right the same way and the upper separates from the lower entirely.
steps.prose: Worth doing for a real clean: it gives you the buffer tube and the whole lower interior instead of a hinged rifle swinging about while you brush at it.
steps.quote: For convenience, the pivot pin may be pushed from left to right (just like the take down pin) and the upper receiver will then be separated from the lower receiver.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Field Stripping Your Firearm, printed pp.14-19

steps.title: Carrier out — don't let the bolt drop
steps.action: Pull the charging handle back SLOWLY and draw the bolt carrier assembly out, keeping hold of it so the bolt does not fall out of the front as it comes.
steps.prose: The bolt slides freely in an extended carrier and lands on its lugs. Slowly, with a hand under it.
steps.quote: Slowly pull the charging handle back and remove the bolt carrier assembly. Be careful not to drop the bolt out as the charging handle comes back.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Field Stripping Your Firearm, printed pp.14-19

steps.title: Charging handle out through the keyway
steps.action: Draw the charging handle back until its ears line up with the keyway in the upper — about 4.4 inches out — and lift it up and out.
steps.prose: Bushmaster gives the actual figure, which saves the usual fumbling for the one position where it drops free.
steps.quote: When the charging handle is extended out approximately 4.4" from the upper receiver, the ears on the charging handle should be lined up and can slide up through the keyway.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Field Stripping Your Firearm, printed pp.14-19

steps.title: ⛔ Bore FROM THE BREECH — and no foam cleaners
steps.action: Run a properly sized bore brush in from the BREECH, never the muzzle, then wipe the fouling out with a bore patch. Repeat until nothing comes out. ⛔ No foam cleaners, and no strong ammonia or alkaline solvents.
steps.prose: ⛔ "DO NOT USE FOAM CLEANERS" is printed three separate times in this book, including inside the numbered warranty limitations. That is a maker telling you it has seen the damage.
steps.quote: Use a properly sized bore brush to remove fouling from the bore. Always run the brush in from the breach and not the muzzle.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Cleaning and Lubricating Your Firearm, printed pp.20-21
steps.warn: If improper solvents are used, damage to the firearm finish may occur. Use of strong ammonia or alkaline type solvents is not recommended your firearm. DO NOT USE FOAM CLEANERS!

steps.title: Chamber brush built for the chamber, not the bore
steps.action: Use a chamber brush specifically designed for the 5.56 NATO chamber to take all the fouling out, then wipe with a chamber patch and repeat until clean. Light lubricant on the bore afterwards.
steps.prose: A bore brush is the wrong diameter for a chamber and skates past the shoulder and the lug recesses, which is exactly where the carbon is.
steps.quote: Use a chamber brush specifically designed for the 5.56 NATO chamber to remove all fouling from the chamber.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Cleaning and Lubricating Your Firearm, printed pp.20-21

steps.title: Every carbon site Bushmaster names, by name
steps.action: Take all the carbon residue off the extractor, the bolt, the bolt carrier key, the firing pin, the firing pin chamber, the carrier, the charging handle and the upper receiver. Pipe cleaners and cotton swabs reach most of it.
steps.prose: That list IS the fouling map of a direct-impingement rifle, and the carrier key and firing pin chamber are the two nobody reaches without a pipe cleaner.
steps.quote: Remove all carbon residue from the extractor, bolt, bolt carrier key, firing pin, firing pin chamber, carrier, charging handle, and upper receiver.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Cleaning and Lubricating Your Firearm, printed pp.20-21

steps.title: ⛔ Every 500 rounds — or 100 on poor ammunition
steps.action: Field strip, clean and lubricate at least every 500 rounds. Some poor quality foreign ammunition needs it after 100. And always after exposure to water, dirt, sand or extreme humidity.
steps.prose: ⛔ Bushmaster explains the interval rather than asserting it: excessive carbon build-up is the leading cause of malfunctions in any AR type rifle. The 100-round figure is the maker's own, not a rule of thumb.
steps.aside: Some poor quality foreign ammunition may require thorough cleaning after just 100 rounds in order to maintain reliable functioning.
steps.quote: We recommend that your firearm be field stripped, cleaned, and lubricated at least every 500 rounds for proper functioning.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Cleaning and Lubricating Your Firearm, printed pp.20-21

steps.title: Light lube outside, no fingerprints left on it
steps.action: After cleaning, coat the external parts lightly with a firearms-specific lubricant — a quality dry lube for the exterior metal — and wipe the fingerprints off.
steps.prose: Finger moisture is acidic and starts corrosion on a phosphated or anodised surface within days in a humid house.
steps.quote: In any case, do not leave any obvious finger prints on the metal surfaces as finger moisture may lead to corrosion.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Cleaning and Lubricating Your Firearm, printed pp.20-21

steps.title: Field strip complete — the bolt and buffer are the deep job
steps.action: Upper, lower, bolt carrier group and charging handle. Bushmaster also publishes the bolt strip, the buffer and the magazine, and those are the DEEP CLEAN below.
steps.prose: ⛔ Past that, Bushmaster's own line is that further disassembly voids the warranty and goes to a gunsmith or a Bushmaster armorer. It also asks for PERIODIC maintenance by an armorer every year or 10,000 rounds, whichever comes first — that is not an owner task.
steps.quote: Never disassemble your firearm beyond what has been described herein. To do so will void the warranty.
steps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Field Stripping Your Firearm, printed pp.14-19

deepSteps.title: Bolt extended, then the firing pin retaining pin
deepSteps.action: Make sure the bolt is forward in the carrier, then take out the firing pin retaining pin. It looks like a cotter pin and only goes through one side of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: Knowing it is one-sided saves people trying to drive it straight through and bending it.
deepSteps.quote: Next remove the firing pin retaining pin. (It looks like a cotter pin and is designed to only go through one side of the bolt carrier.)
deepSteps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Field Stripping Your Firearm, printed pp.14-19

deepSteps.title: Bolt IN, firing pin out the rear
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt into the carrier body, then let the firing pin slide out of the rear of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: Tip the carrier so it falls into your hand rather than onto the bench — the tip is the part that matters.
deepSteps.aside: Remove the firing pin. It will slide out to the rear of the carrier.
deepSteps.quote: Push the bolt into the carrier body.
deepSteps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Field Stripping Your Firearm, printed pp.14-19

deepSteps.title: Cam pin 90 degrees, then the bolt out
deepSteps.action: Turn the bolt cam pin 90 degrees and lift it out of the carrier, then take the bolt out of the carrier body.
deepSteps.prose: The pin sits under the gas key and will not lift until the bolt is pushed home — which is why the previous step comes first.
deepSteps.quote: Turn the bolt cam pin 90 degrees and remove it from the carrier.
deepSteps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Field Stripping Your Firearm, printed pp.14-19

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Extractor — and one thing that stays put
deepSteps.action: Push on the back of the extractor to take the pressure off its roll pin and drive the pin out with a correctly sized punch. ⛔ Do NOT try to remove the rubber grommet from the extractor spring.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The grommet is a tuned part of the extractor's spring rate, not a seal. Pulling it out changes how hard the claw grips and it does not go back the same.
deepSteps.quote: Do not attempt to remove the rubber grommet from the extractor spring.
deepSteps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Field Stripping Your Firearm, printed pp.14-19

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Buffer and action spring — the hammer must be cocked
deepSteps.action: Push the buffer assembly in slightly while depressing the buffer retainer, then let the buffer and spring slide past the retainer SLOWLY. The buffer has three flats on it — sit one of them over the retainer and it comes out easily. The hammer must be cocked so it is not in the way.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ The spring is long and under load. "Slowly" is the whole instruction; released, it launches the buffer out of the tube at face height.
deepSteps.quote: Note that the buffer assembly has three flats on it. It is easier to remove the assembly if one of the buffer assembly flats is positioned over the buffer retainer.
deepSteps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Field Stripping Your Firearm, printed pp.14-19

deepSteps.title: Magazine apart for cleaning
deepSteps.action: Put a tool into the hole in the magazine floorplate and lever the edge of the base up just enough to slide it off the rear of the magazine. Then take the spring and follower out.
deepSteps.prose: Keep a thumb on the floorplate as it goes — the spring is compressed. Note the follower's orientation before it leaves the tube.
deepSteps.aside: You may now remove the spring and follower from the magazine.
deepSteps.quote: In order to disassemble the magazine for cleaning, place a tool into the hole in the magazine floorplate.
deepSteps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Field Stripping Your Firearm, printed pp.14-19

deepSteps.title: ⛔ REBUILD: gas ring gaps STAGGERED, cam pin IN
deepSteps.action: Before the bolt goes back into the carrier, check the three gas ring gaps are staggered and NOT in line. Then the cam pin — and check it is in correctly. Lightly lubricate all metal parts as it goes together and wipe the excess off.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ Bushmaster states the consequence of a missing cam pin in plain words: the firearm can fire AND MAY EXPLODE. This is the one check that is not optional. Inspect for wear and cracks while everything is apart.
deepSteps.aside: Prior to assembling the bolt into the bolt carrier assembly, ensure that the three gas ring gaps are staggered and NOT in alignment. The gaps must be staggered for proper functioning.
deepSteps.quote: The firearm can fire and may explode if the cam pin is not installed into the bolt carrier.
deepSteps.cite: Bushmaster XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual — XM15-E2S Safety + Operating Manual, 2025 revision — Reassembly of your firearm, printed pp.22-23

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: ⛔ Brush in from the BREECH, never the muzzle
5.56 NATO chamber brush — not a bore brush
Light lubricant on the bore when it is clean

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Extractor, bolt, carrier key, firing pin and its chamber
Pipe cleaners and swabs for the key and the pin recess
⛔ Gas ring gaps STAGGERED on reassembly

cleaning.name: RECEIVERS
tasks: Charging handle and the whole upper interior
⛔ NO foam cleaners; no strong ammonia or alkaline solvents
Light dry lube outside; no fingerprints left on

cleaning.name: INTERVAL
tasks: ⛔ Every 500 rounds — 100 on poor foreign ammunition
Always after water, dirt, sand or extreme humidity
Armorer service every year or 10,000 rounds — not an owner job

reassembly: Reassemble in the reverse order of the strip.
⛔ Before the bolt goes into the carrier, stagger the three gas ring gaps.
⛔ Confirm the cam pin is installed correctly — a rifle fired without it may explode.
Lightly lubricate all metal parts and remove the excess.
Inspect for wear, cracks and other deficiencies as it goes together; anything found goes to a gunsmith or armorer before the rifle is used again.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber verified visually AND physically, muzzle safe. Cycle the charging handle and confirm the bolt returns fully into battery. Selector to SAFE and pull the trigger — the hammer must not fall. Selector to FIRE and pull — it should. Check both pins are seated. ⛔ And confirm the cam pin is in before anything else: Bushmaster's own words are that the rifle can fire and may explode without it.
